title: Careless Love
origin: American folk blues from the Southern states; a floating traditional song in oral circulation well before 1900, later a staple of the New Orleans and vaudeville blues repertoire

pd.detail: Anonymous American folk blues, in oral circulation in the Southern states through the nineteenth century and well established before 1900; no identifiable author survives. W. C. Handy's 'Loveless Love' (1921) is his own copyrighted reworking of this older song, not its source.
pd.sourceEdition: The traditional sixteen-bar folk-blues version common to American folk and early-jazz practice; no single printed edition is claimed as the transcription source. Deliberately NOT Handy's 'Loveless Love' (1921) and not any later recorded arrangement.
pd.notes: Melody and changes only; no lyrics. The traditional common-practice version is encoded rather than any single copyrighted arrangement of it. Some old-time variants of this song are sung in 3/4; that version is NOT encoded here.

notes: Sixteen-bar folk-blues form built from four four-bar lines: each line is sung across the first two or three bars with an instrumental answer filling the rest. Changes are the standard ones -- I I V7 V7 | V7 V7 I I | I I7 IV IV | I V7 I I. Line 1 rises to the 5th and hangs on the 2nd over the V7; line 2 descends from the 5th through the b7 of the V7 and resolves to the tonic; line 3 is the high point, reaching the octave and falling through the b7 over the I7-IV move; line 4 falls to the tonic through the leading tone below it. Straight 4/4: the shuffle subdivision is carried by feel=swing, not by the grid, and no triplets are written. Some old-time folk variants of this song are sung in 3/4; that version is NOT encoded here. Intro and outro are chord-only turnaround vamps -- arrangement, not tune -- and deliberately carry no melody. Melody confidence is medium: the four-line contour and the changes are solid, individual passing notes are a reconstruction.
